sources.entry: C: _How to create an OS from scratch_
How to create an OS from scratch

summary.one_liner: A step-by-step tutorial for building a small x86 operating system from scratch in assembly and C, starting from a custom boot sector, though the author marks it as an abandoned project.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a learning course organized as numbered folders that build on each other in order. It covers booting without GRUB from a custom boot sector, entering 32-bit mode, jumping from assembly to C, interrupt handling, screen output and keyboard input, and a tiny basic libc. Per the README's strategy list, the items marked DONE are boot, 32-bit mode, assembly-to-C, interrupts, screen/keyboard, and a basic libc. Memory management, a filesystem, a shell, user mode, a text editor, and multitasking are listed as planned but not done. Each lesson has a short README stating prerequisites and goals, plus commented code files. The README says it is concise and has little theory.
use_cases: learning how operating systems boot from scratch
following a step-by-step OS development course
learning x86 assembly and 32-bit mode transition
writing a custom bootloader without GRUB
studying interrupt handling and keyboard input at a low level
notable: Lessons are small numbered folders meant to be followed in order, each with a short README and commented code
Builds a custom boot sector without relying on GRUB
Covers the path from 16-bit boot to 32-bit mode and assembly-to-C jumps
Minimal theory; the author points readers to external sources like the OSDev wiki
caveats: The author states this is an old, abandoned project and recommends more modern, authoritative sources for OS design
Several planned features (memory management, filesystem, shell, user mode, multitasking) are not yet done
